3383.title: [Follow-up] Deliver tracked-variable/v1 contract omitted by #3376
3383.body:
<!-- follow-up-depth: 2 -->
## Why
PR #3376 merged only an issue ledger and did not implement issue #3371; both verifiers returned **FAIL**. This follow-up addresses the remaining gaps with improved task structure.

## Source
- Original PR: #3376
- Parent issue: #3371

## Contract preserved from parent #3371

The version literal is `tracked-variable/v1` (slash), while the filename is `tracked-variable-v1.schema.json`. Follow parent #3371 and its cited B3 §3.1 and Ready INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE §D for the wire shape; do not invent a reduced evidence-only schema. The required embedded `evidence` must conform to the existing `evidence-object/v1` schema, and required dual `provenance.document` and `provenance.mirror` objects must preserve the B3 contract. Document `clause-variable/v1` as the same wire shape with `ontology_family: "clause"`. Do not implement consumer extractors or replace the existing evidence schema.

## Tasks
- [ ] Set `schema_version` const to `tracked-variable/v1`; validate embedded `evidence` against `evidence-object/v1` and include the required document/mirror provenance contract.
- [ ] Document the clause-variable vocabulary alias and its `ontology_family: "clause"` mapping.
- [ ] Add the tracked-variable schema at `docs/contracts/schemas/tracked-variable-v1.schema.json`, defining the tracked-variable-v1 object and making `evidence` a required field.
- [ ] Create the normative specification document at `docs/contracts/tracked-variable-v1.md` describing the tracked-variable-v1 contract and its required fields.
- [ ] Add tracked-variable fixture files under `tests/fixtures/backplane/`: `valid_tracked_variable.json` with the expected `evidence` key and `invalid_tracked_variable_missing_evidence.json` without that key.
- [ ] Update `tests/contracts/test_backplane_schemas.py` to register `tracked-variable-v1.schema.json` and add `test_tracked_variable_fixture_validates` that validates the new fixture and checks that the missing-`evidence` case fails validation.
- [ ] Extend `scripts/validate_run_contract.py` with a `--tracked-variables` CLI flag wired into the existing schema validation options.

## Sync delivery task
- [x] Add sync-manifest entries for `docs/contracts/schemas/tracked-variable-v1.schema.json` and `docs/contracts/tracked-variable-v1.md` in `.github/sync-manifest.yml`. Implemented in PR #3385. The former inferred restriction was an automation classification error: AGENTS.md explicitly requires consumer-facing artifacts to have manifest coverage, and this manifest is not an executable workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The schema file contains `"const": "tracked-variable/v1"` in the schema_version property definition, includes a `$ref` to `evidence-object/v1` schema for the evidence field, and defines both `provenance.document` and `provenance.mirror` as required object properties. The normative spec includes a section titled "Clause Variable Alias" that documents the ontology_family mapping.
- [ ] The test `test_tracked_variable_fixture_validates` must include an assertion that validates `valid_tracked_variable.json` passes validation. Create a comment in the test code documenting that removing the `evidence` key from the valid fixture causes this assertion to fail (verified during development). Include both positive and negative test cases in the same test function.
- [ ] The file `docs/contracts/schemas/tracked-variable-v1.schema.json` exists and defines a top-level schema for `tracked-variable-v1` in which `evidence` is listed in the schema's `required` array.
- [ ] The file `docs/contracts/tracked-variable-v1.md` exists and explicitly documents the `tracked-variable-v1` contract, including that `evidence` is a required field.
- [ ] The fixture file `tests/fixtures/backplane/valid_tracked_variable.json` exists and contains an `evidence` key, and the fixture file `tests/fixtures/backplane/invalid_tracked_variable_missing_evidence.json` exists and does not contain an `evidence` key.
- [ ] The test module `tests/contracts/test_backplane_schemas.py` registers `tracked-variable-v1.schema.json` in the schema validation coverage and defines a test named `test_tracked_variable_fixture_validates`.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/contracts/test_backplane_schemas.py::test_tracked_variable_fixture_validates -q` exits with status code 0.
- [ ] The test `tests/contracts/test_backplane_schemas.py::test_tracked_variable_fixture_validates` asserts both that `tests/fixtures/backplane/valid_tracked_variable.json` validates successfully against `tracked-variable-v1.schema.json` and that `tests/fixtures/backplane/invalid_tracked_variable_missing_evidence.json` fails validation because `evidence` is required.
- [ ] Running `python scripts/validate_run_contract.py --help` prints a usage/help message that includes the literal option name `--tracked-variables` and exits with status code 0.

## Implementation Notes
Use the repository's existing contract/schema patterns for new schema and spec files so `tracked-variable-v1` matches the established layout and naming conventions.

Target these files directly:
- `docs/contracts/schemas/tracked-variable-v1.schema.json`
- `docs/contracts/tracked-variable-v1.md`
- `tests/fixtures/backplane/valid_tracked_variable.json`
- `tests/fixtures/backplane/invalid_tracked_variable_missing_evidence.json`
- `tests/contracts/test_backplane_schemas.py`
- `scripts/validate_run_contract.py`

For tests, add explicit positive and negative coverage tied to the `evidence` requirement rather than only registering the schema generally.

For the CLI change, wire `--tracked-variables` into the existing validation option flow so it appears in `--help` output and participates in the normal schema-validation path.

## Notes
<details>
<summary>Advisory items (non-blocking)</summary>

</details>

<details>
<summary>Background (previous attempt context)</summary>

- The previous PR diff contained unrelated configuration and ledger changes rather than the actual tracked-variable artifacts. This failed because the changes did not target the required files or include implementations conforming to the acceptance criteria. Focus on producing the specific deliverables in this issue rather than generic repository or ledger updates.
- No modifications were made to tests, CLI, or sync files relevant to tracked-variable-v1, even though comments referenced the task as done. Ensure artifact creation and direct code changes are visible in the diff, with files present and tests explicitly covering the new functionality.

</details>

3624.title: [Follow-up] Update the stranske/Template repository to include (PR #3564)
3624.body:
## Why

PR #3564 addressed issue #3423, but verification returned **CONCERNS**: the three `priority:*` labels are defined only as a literal in `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`, so a repository created from `stranske/Template` starts without them and the opener cannot select its issues until bootstrap repairs it. The labels need one checked-in source of truth that the existing label sync (`.github/workflows/maint-69-sync-labels.yml`, which already targets `stranske/Template` through the consumer registry) delivers, and bootstrap must read that same source rather than a second copy.

## Source
- Original PR: #3564
- Parent issue: #3423

## Scope

Workflows repository only: `.github/labels-core.yml`, `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`, `tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py`, and one new helper script under `scripts/`.

<!-- follow-up-depth: 1 -->

## Non-Goals

- Do not edit the `stranske/Template` repository directly; the existing `maint-69-sync-labels.yml` sync delivers `.github/labels-core.yml` there.
- Do not change the colors or descriptions of the three labels; reuse the current values from `PRIORITY_LABELS` in `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`.
- Do not modify `.github/workflows/maint-69-sync-labels.yml` or any other protected workflow file.
- Do not populate a PR description automatically; the helper only writes a file.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `priority:high`, `priority:normal` and `priority:low` entries to `.github/labels-core.yml`, using the exact `color` and `description` values currently in `PRIORITY_LABELS` in `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`.
- [ ] Change `PRIORITY_LABELS` in `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py` so it is loaded from `.github/labels-core.yml` (filtering names that start with `priority:`) instead of being a hard-coded literal, and fail loudly if any of the three names is missing from that file.
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py` asserting that the three priority labels in `.github/labels-core.yml` are equal (name, color, description) to `PRIORITY_LABELS`, so the sync source and bootstrap cannot drift.
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py` for the repository-from-template path: given a label inventory that already contains all three labels, `apply_priority_labels` creates nothing and reports success.
- [ ] Add `scripts/capture_bootstrap_label_tests.py`, which runs `pytest tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py -q` and writes the combined stdout/stderr to a path passed as `--out` (default `artifacts/bootstrap-label-tests.txt`), exiting with pytest's exit code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/labels-core.yml` contains exactly one entry each for `priority:high`, `priority:normal` and `priority:low`, with colors `b60205`, `fbca04` and `0e8a16` respectively.
- [ ] `grep -n '"color": "b60205"' scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py` returns no match (the literal is gone).
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py -q` passes, including the two new tests.
- [ ] Deliberate break: changing the `priority:low` color in `.github/labels-core.yml` makes the drift test fail; reverting it makes the test pass again.
- [ ] `python scripts/capture_bootstrap_label_tests.py --out /tmp/out.txt` exits 0 and `/tmp/out.txt` is non-empty and contains the pytest summary line (for example `passed`).

## Implementation Notes

- `.github/labels-core.yml` is a YAML list of `{name, color, description}` mappings; quote the colors as the existing entries do.
- `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py` currently imports only the standard library; if PyYAML is unavailable in that script's runtime, parse the file with the same loader used elsewhere in `scripts/` rather than adding a new dependency.
- `tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py::test_priority_labels_are_literal_and_match_review_uploader` may need its name and assertion updated so it checks equality with the review uploader's labels rather than literalness.
